newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan unveils package to spur stock market.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan unveils package to spur stock market.

text.p: Pakistan's caretaker government unveiled a package on Monday to stimulate the country's stock market, allowing companies to repurchase up to 10 percent of their own shares.

Caretaker Prime Minister Meraj Khalid's finance and economic affairs adviser Shahid Javed Burki told a news conference after a cabinet meeting that bonus shares would be exempted from a 10 percent withholding tax, and earnings from rights issues from income tax.

"Not only will this be helpful to the corporate sector, but this will put capital market development on the right track," Burki said as he announced the package of incentives aimed at reviving sentiment at Pakistan's three sagging bourses.
"The cabinet approved a number of measures to revive the stock market, thus promoting capital formation and increasing the inflow of portfolio funds from abroad," a government statement said.
Burki said the government had asked the four provincial governments to rationalise stamp duty on share transactions and reduce it to the lowest level now applicable in Sindh province.
Income from mutual funds and units of state-run National Investment Trust, an open-ended mutual fund, will be exempted from income tax, he said.

Burki said companies wishing to repurchase treasury stock would have to announce their intentions through a tender offer to be published in newspapers. "The process that we propose to follow will be a very transparent one."
Insurance companies will be exempted from capital gains on shares traded on the stock exchanges and income from trading shares will be exempted from the tax on turnover, he said.
He said the package had been approved after consulting the presidents and directors of the Karachi, Lahore and Islamabad stock exchanges.
These are all positive developments that will have a positive impact on the market, an executive of Khadim Ali Shah Bokhari and Co said.
